card.name: Numbers and counts in lab-based stopping criteria
card.fires_on: Small count or duration words and numbers (such as 'three', '2', 'for' before a number of days or hours) in rules that set lab thresholds or time spans for holding or stopping a drug.

modes.label: Multiples of normal
modes.description: The number word in 'three or more times the upper limit of normal' for liver enzyme rises.

modes.label: Occasions or duration
modes.description: A number or the gap before a duration that says how often or how long a lab abnormality must last.

modes.description: Words that mark an abnormality as lasting, before a time span.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward the word 'criteria' or 'conditions', as in a set of conditions that must be met.
card.plain: It fires inside dose-adjustment rules where a lab value must reach a number or last a set time, as if a criterion is coming.
